newsitem.title: JORDAN: Japan-Jordan fertiliser plant officially launched.
newsitem.headline: Japan-Jordan fertiliser plant officially launched.

text.p: A joint Japanese-Jordanian project to produce ammonium phosphates and compound fertiliser was officially launched on Saturday, industry officials said.
They said Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan inaugurated the $85 million plant, built by Japanese Shiyoda engineering company at a site close to Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba.
The plant has produced 7,000 tonnes since it began test production early last month.

It is expected to build up production gradually over the next year to its maximum capacity of 300,000 tonnes of mixed fertilisers annually. It will use 80,000 tonnes of phosphoric acid annually, equivalent to 260,000 tonnes of raw phosphate.
The Nippon-Jordan Fertiliser Company is a joint venture with Jordan Phosphates Mines Company, Arab Potash and a Japanese consortium which owns 60 percent of the venture.
Another $170 million Jordanian-Indian joint venture to export 200,000 tonnes of phosphoric acid to a fertilizer complex in India is expected to come on stream soon.
